answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks through hardware-rooted remote attestation, binding each agent to an isolated enclave thread via silicon monotonic counters. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital expenditure of acquiring separate physical hardware chips per identity, ensuring provisioning costs spiral linearly and rendering zero-cost cloning a fable. However, this approach centralizes trust in hardware vendors and remains susceptible to undisclosed side-channel vulnerabilities.
